Sports.title: José Mourinho reveals he signed contract to succeed Alex Ferguson at Manchester United in 2013
Sports.content:
José Mourinho has revealed he signed a contract to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson as Manchester United manager in 2013 only to tearfully renege on the deal and return to Chelsea.

The football world was rocked when the Scottish great announced he was retiring having overseen a 13th Premier League title triumph during a spell of unrivalled dominance at Old Trafford.

United have failed to return to the top of the English game since Ferguson stepped down, with his successor, David Moyes, sacked after only 10 months in charge.

Mourinho was later brought in, spending two and a half years in charge from 2016, but revealed in a new Netflix documentary about his life that he had agreed to come earlier.

“I go to Chelsea in 2013 but in that period there is something nobody knows,” the Portuguese said in the documentary, which is entitled Mourinho. “I think I can say because I don’t hurt anyone with the truth, and I think the objective of this work that we are doing is to tell the truth. When I left Real Madrid, I signed with Manchester United to go to Manchester United after Sir Alex.”

Mourinho continued: “I was, of course, very flattered, because Manchester United has an incredible appeal. When I say Real Madrid is the biggest club in the world, I have to say that Manchester United is very, very close.

double quotation mark He phoned me and he was crying. He says: ‘Alex, I can’t take it – I’ve given my word to Chelsea.’ Sir Alex Ferguson

“But one thing is love for football, and another thing is love for a certain club. I think this is more powerful than love for football and, fundamentally, after Real Madrid, I needed to feel that I’m loved.”

Ferguson was one of the footballing figures interviewed for the new documentary and admits he was under the illusion Mourinho was accepting the offer, only for the situation to change in a matter of hours.

“Early evening he phoned me and he was crying,” the United great said. “And he says: ‘Alex, I can’t take it – I’ve given my word to Chelsea, and I’m not going to break my word.’ The reason he gave to me I could understand, but I was disappointed.”

Mourinho had a strong bond with Chelsea after leading them to two Premier League titles, an FA Cup and two League Cups during his first spell.

View image in fullscreen Alex Ferguson’s long spell as Manchester United manager ended in May 2013. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

The Portuguese parked differences with the Chelsea owner, Roman Abramovich, to return to Stamford Bridge after leaving Real Madrid, winning another league crown and League Cup before being sacked in December 2015.

“For me to lose the chance to be the coach to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson was dramatic, but I don’t regret because it was a decision that I made with my heart,” Mourinho, now back in charge of Real Madrid, said.

“And I think it is nature that says something that when you do something for love, you are never doing anything wrong. I think it’s nature. I did it for love.

“I went back with the feeling of, yes, I go home, but with big responsibility because what I did before is history, and you don’t want to destroy your legacy.”

Sports.title: La Liga president Javier Tebas says ‘Infantino era is over’ at Fifa
Sports.content:
Javier Tebas says Gianni Infantino’s position as Fifa president is untenable, claiming he is “destroying the very essence of football” while calling for reform at the highest levels of the game.

The La Liga president, who is a longstanding and vociferous critic of the current Fifa regime, said “the Infantino era is over” and called for control of the game to be expanded beyond the current “elite”.

While Tebas’s remarks will surprise no one within the game, they maintain the drumbeat of criticism directed against Infantino following his determination to continue in post despite his secret and subsequently quashed plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.

In an interview with French newspaper Le Monde, Tebas repeated his call for Infantino to resign, an appeal first made after the World Cup but before the sell-off scandal. “For me, Gianni Infantino’s time has long since passed,” he said.

“I’m not saying this because of recent events; I have noticed this style of management for a long time, though everyone else seems to be discovering it only now.

“Gianni Infantino is not someone who contributes to the growth of football. On the contrary, his projects are destroying the very essence of the sport: the national leagues.

“Football is not limited to the elite. For me, the Infantino era is over. What remains to be seen is when that will take effect and how the succession will unfold. I hope it is not just a matter of swapping out some people for others, but of a genuine overhaul.”

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino has received the backing of Fifa in spite of Uefa’s threat to boycott all its tournaments. Photograph: Sam Corum/PA

Infantino is battling to stay in post despite an increasingly coordinated attempt by European football officials and others to unseat the 56-year-old Swiss. Uefa has made it clear they regard Infantino’s continued leadership of world football as untenable, the Norwegian FA has called for the president to stand down and a number of European associations have withdrawn letters endorsing Infantino for another term at the head of Fifa.

Uefa confirmed on Saturday that a “departure payment” had been made to a female employee who is alleged to have been in a relationship with Infantino while he was the organisation’s general secretary more than a decade ago.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Daily Telegraph reported on Friday night that the woman received a six-figure sum after the alleged relationship, allegations Fifa dismissed as “categorically untrue”.

On Saturday night, Fifa published a statement accusing Infantino’s critics of attempting to remove him from office before the presidential election next March. “Those who do not have the support of Fifa’s member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through Fifa’s established democratic processes,” the statement read.

Infantino has also garnered support from prominent nations outside Europe, including the World Cup co-host Mexico and the finalists Argentina. Uefa say a proposed boycott of all Fifa tournaments remains in prospect, with the women’s Under-20 World Cup due to start in Poland on 5 September.

Sports.title: Hibernian stun Rangers at Ibrox while O’Neill misses Høgh treble in Celtic win
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes suffered a damaging home debut as Rangers manager with a 2-1 Premiership defeat to Hibernian compounded by striker Youssef Chermiti being carried off the pitch on a stretcher.

David Gray’s side took the lead in the 12th minute with a Josh Campbell penalty after the video assistant referee (VAR) had flagged up that Vanja Dragojevic, making his first Rangers start after signing from Partizan Belgrade, had fouled Jason Kerr in the area.

There was more woe before the break when Chermiti, subject to a failed bid by Galatasaray for a reported club record fee of £22million, having to go off after picking up an injury.

Rangers pushed forward relentlessly and were rewarded in the 85th minute when the Hibs defender Miguel Chaiwa turned the ball past the goalkeeper Raphael Sallinger.

However, in the third minute of added time, the substitute Callum Wright guided a shot into the far corner for a stunning win.

With Celtic and St Mirren both on six points from two games, Rangers are five behind with McInnes looking for his first win after three matches in the Ibrox hot seat.

Kasper Høgh scored a hat-trick, his first goals for Celtic, as the Scottish champions made light of the absence of their manager Martin O’Neill with a 5-1 win at Kilmarnock. O’Neill missed the trip to Rugby Park after what the club had said earlier this week was a “small procedure” in hospital.

No details were given about O’Neill’s operation, which came after the veteran Northern Irish manager took charge of Celtic’s win against Dundee in their first game of the season. But the club’s assistant manager, Shaun Maloney, speaking before Sunday’s kick-off, said O’Neill was on the mend. “He is doing better again,” Maloney told Sky Sports. “He came to the team hotel and spoke to the players but he just needs an extra few days.”

View image in fullscreen Celtic’s Kasper Høgh scores the first of his three goals against Kilmarnock. Photograph: Robert Perry/PA

O’Neill’s mood would doubtless have been improved by the performance of his side, with Celtic 3-0 ahead before half-time thanks to Høgh. The Danish striker, who joined in July from Bodø/Glimt, needed less than a minute to score his first Celtic goal, heading in at the back post from a cross by Arne Engels.

Høgh doubled Celtic’s lead in the 33rd minute, with Camilo Durán seizing on Johnly Yfeko’s pass out of defence. He combined with Benjamin Nygren to work the ball to Høgh on the left edge of the box, with the forward finishing well.

Two minutes later, Høgh had his hat-trick. Nygren slipping the ball right for Durán, whose cross took the Kilmarnock goalkeeper Max Stryjek out of play, with Høgh nodding into an empty net.

Celtic extended their lead early in the second half after they were effectively gifted a fourth goal by Stryjek. His pass out of defence went straight to Nygren in front of goal and his shot into the top corner made it 4-0.

Michael Schjønning-Larsen pulled a goal back for Kilmarnock in the 56th minute after finishing a well-worked move. But Celtic went four goals ahead again when Luke McCowan, moments after coming on, volleyed in from close range 15 minutes from time after Kilmarnock made a mess of trying to clear the ball from a corner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Celtic’s assistant manager Shaun Maloney took charge with Martin O’Neill still recovering from a procedure in hospital. Photograph: Robert Perry/PA

Three Hearts summer signings were on target as Wouter Vrancken belatedly got his reign up and running with a 4-0 win over Dundee United. The Belgian had suffered four consecutive defeats – three in Europe – since replacing Derek McInnes in June, but his new-look team tore United apart in their first home league game of the season.

Tom Renaud, Calvin Miller and Josh McPake all marked their first league outings at Tynecastle with goals, while last season’s talisman Cláudio Braga broke his duck for the campaign.

Hearts made a fast start as Renaud, a few days after notching against Benfica, unleashed a ferocious strike beyond Jack Walton from just short of 30 yards after being teed up by Braga in the fourth minute.

View image in fullscreen Josh McPake turns away after scoring Hearts’ fourth goal against Dundee United. Photograph: Malcolm Mackenzie/Getty Images

The home side were gifted the chance to double their lead when VAR spotted Daniel Bennie wrestling Jamie McCart to the ground in the box. Miller stepped up to fire the penalty straight down the middle.

Hearts killed off any hopes of a United fightback in the 56th minute when Braga drilled in a low angled shot from 12 yards out after being set up by Sabah Kerjota. McPake then marked his first competitive start for Hearts with his first goal as he tucked a clinical low finish beyond Walton after playing a one-two with Braga on the left of the box.

In Sunday’s other 3pm kick-off, Motherwell drew 0-0 at home to Falkirk.

On Saturday, Dundee beat Aberdeen 2-0 thanks to goals from Joe Westley and Joe Bevan while St Mirren edged St Johnstone 1-0 courtesy of Killian Phillips’ penalty.

Sports.title: Iraola says Liverpool have work to do as familiar frailties in defence prove costly
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola told his Liverpool team they have work to do after ­squandering a 2-0 lead against Monaco to lose a second successive pre-season friendly.

The former Bournemouth coach last managed a game at Anfield almost exactly a year ago in the memorable opener to the 2025-26 Premier League season, a game the Cherries were unfortunate to lose 4-2. Now on his debut in the home dugout, Iraola saw his team produce a similarly open display and lose again. It became clear Liverpool’s longstanding defensive frailties are still to be eliminated.

Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz scored in the first half as the hosts exhibited some free-flowing ­football, but Monaco dominated a ­second half that became fragmented as Iraola and Monaco’s Filipe Luís made wholesale changes.

“As soon as we have made some changes they start to get tired, we cannot sustain that level, so we have work to do,” Iraola told LFCTV on Liverpool’s “frustrating” regression after a bright start. “They were much better in the second half, in the same way we were better in the first half.”

After Liverpool beat Wrexham and Sunderland during a pre-season tour to the US, a 4-2 defeat against Leeds brought back memories of the struggles of last season. This result will cause some concerns with transfer activity dragging.

Ronald Araújo is at least due to arrive on loan from Barcelona. Although that deal is not yet complete and Alexis Mac Allister is still to return from World Cup duty, Iraola’s team to face Monaco was strong, with Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, and Lewis Koumas, 20, the only fringe players to start if you exclude Kostas Tsimikas, back from a loan at Roma. Jérémy Jacquet and Curtis Jones were not considered because of fitness doubts, with Iraola at pains not to “rush” Jaquet, who signed from Rennes for £50m, into action after a chequered time with injury.

Iraola said: “Jérémy, we were in doubt whether to pick him today, he should be fine for the next one. Curtis [there is] something wrong with his hip, [it] didn’t make sense to risk [him].”

Wirtz was sharp, testing Lukas Hradecky with an early shot. Isak’s opener on 16 minutes was met with a hearty cheer from the home faithful, perhaps not surprising given it was just the fourth time the Anfield crowd have been able to celebrate an Isak goal, competitive or otherwise.

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola was disappointed after watching Liverpool slip to a second successive friendly defeat. Photograph: Lewis Storey/Danehouse/Getty Images

The strike came after Ryan ­Gravenberch and Dominik ­Szoboszlai’s slick midfield exchange, the former then finding the Swede, who rifled low into the corner. Koumas and Wirtz both squandered presentable chances, but it was soon 2-0 when the German forced home after a ­goalmouth scramble.

Iraola cut a relaxed figure on the touchline throughout and was content with his side’s attacking fluidity. The Spaniard’s preference for a high defensive line was evident throughout, though Alisson was tested far less often than Hradecky until he had to face a 44th-minute penalty after Virgil van Dijk’s trip on Aleksandr Golovin. The Russian stroked home the spot-kick himself to make it 2-1 at the break, giving ­Alisson no chance.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Wataru Endo for Ndukwe and Giorgi Mamardashvili for Alisson were the only half-time substitutions from Iraola, who made more sweeping changes just before the hour, with Rio Ngumoha, Milos Kerkez and the summer signing Víctor Muñoz among those introduced.

By that stage it was 2-2, after Mamardashvili had saved from Mika Biereth only to see the striker tap in the rebound. Monaco’s goals were greeted with eerie silence given there were almost no away fans. There were some groans from home supporters frustrated at seeing their side fritter away a two-goal lead but Ngumoha’s name was sung when he came on.

That Ngumoha was selected on the right wing – Mohamed Salah’s old stomping ground – was lost on nobody, nor was the fact that both the youngster and Muñoz were brought on rather than Federico Chiesa. The Italian did appear after 74 minutes along with Harvey Elliott, who was welcomed warmly back to Anfield after his nightmare on loan at Aston Villa.

Monaco carved out the better chances in the search for the next goal, with Flávio Nazinho firing wide, and Oumar Konaté failing to seize on a good through ball, before their 88th-minute winner stemmed from a corner swung in from the left, which Paris Brunner met with a sweet header.

There was no Anfield roar to push the hosts on to equalise as there would have been in a competitive match, and Liverpool’s side resembled a reserves squad by the end, but it was still a tame finish nonetheless. Only a double-header against Como – the first of which will be played behind closed doors – now remains before Iraola’s competitive debut away at Newcastle on 23 August, with his home league debut coming against Nottingham Forest a week later. The manager will demand an improvement in the next fortnight.

Sports.title: Seesaw draw in Malaysia gives Xabi Alonso food for thought at Chelsea
Sports.content:
Chelsea’s problems mounted as their pre-season tour came to an end in a strangely fiery draw against the Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim. The omens do not look promising with a bloated choice of forwards, echoes of their inexperience and indiscipline last season, and fewer than two weeks for the new manager, Xabi Alonso, to reintegrate key players and work with the entirety of his squad before they kick off the Premier League season against Fulham – managed by his old friend Álvaro Arbeloa – on 24 August.

Alonso, tasked with transforming a club that finished 10th in the Premier League last season into Champions League qualifiers, made 11 changes for the friendly against JDT. He rested players after beating Milan with a strong lineup only 24 hours earlier, 600 miles away.

While the defence and midfield were packed with teenagers, the front three – Estêvão Willian, Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson – would be welcomed by most Premier League clubs, having cost Chelsea more than £100m combined in the past three years.

Delap scored twice from the penalty spot – as many goals in 20 minutes as he managed in the entirety of his first season at Chelsea after joining from Ipswich last summer. The 23-year-old is believed to want to stay and fight for his place, having already proved his Premier League pedigree with 12 top-flight goals for Ipswich. Yet Alonso has so many options: João Pedro, one of the standout strikers last season; the new signing Danny Welbeck; and Jackson, who gave the club something to think about on his loan at Bayern Munich last season.

Emmanuel Emegha arrived recently from sister club Strasbourg, and may well go out on loan. They also still have Marc Guiu on the books.

Mykhailo Mudryk returning unexpectedly early from a drugs ban at the end of July was a curveball, adding to a rich choice of options on the wing including Cole Palmer, Estêvão – looking sharp again on Sunday after an injury that derailed the teenager’s promising first season at Stamford Bridge – and the record signing Morgan Rogers, who frequently played off the left for Aston Villa.

Plenty of time remains before the transfer window closes at the end of the month, but Chelsea’s squad stands at a staggering 41 players, with no European football next season and busy weeks of potential disruption ahead that will not ease Alonso’s stresses.

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap scores Chelsea’s second penalty of the evening. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

The JDT manager, Xisco Muñoz, was known for his fierce passion and aggressive football at Watford, and his players treated the game against Chelsea like a competitive fixture at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium in Johor. They flew into challenges, unsettling Chelsea’s players, competing with an intensity rarely seen in a preseason friendly. The visitors failed to keep tempers in check.

There were several flashpoints throughout the match. Delap and Jackson were needlessly booked for dissent, arguing with the referee about challenges on teammates. Estêvão was lucky not to be sent off after kicking out when he felt he was denied a penalty – instead shown a yellow card.

Geovany Quenda came off the bench and was also booked for launching into an entirely unnecessary challenge, as though settling a score. Sixteen-year-old Reggie Watson was booked in stoppage time, making it five yellow cards.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea received 11 red cards last season – twice as many as any other side and a club record – and Alonso has diverged from the owners’ policy of signing young by adding Welbeck, 35, and Jordan Henderson, 36. The club have not fielded a player over 30 since Thiago Silva, then 39, left in May 2024, but it might take more than a couple of veterans to sort the problem out.

JDT took the lead when they caught Chelsea on a break and Arif Aiman – known in these parts as the ‘Asian Messi’ – scored from a rapid move. Delap levelled just before half-time, then gave Chelsea the lead just after the hour. But JDT equalised three minutes later from Óscar Arribas’s heavily deflected free kick, then retook the lead when Bérgson finished into the bottom corner from distance with four minutes remaining. Mudryk, on in the 87th minute, produced the awkward cross that forced Antonio Glauder’s own goal with a minute on the clock, to avoid an embarrassing defeat.

Chelsea return to London after a punishing schedule. Their last three games were in three countries over five days: Juventus in Hong Kong, Milan in Indonesia and JDT in Malaysia – the last two in successive days, their plane landing in Malaysia at 3am on the day of the game.

Alonso has only two weeks – and one final friendly against Real Sociedad on Saturday – to work with the £117m signing Rogers, the injury-prone captain Reece James and the disgruntled star Enzo Fernández, all due back at the club’s Cobham training ground this week following extended World Cup breaks. Then the season will kick off – and the fun and games will really begin.

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Digne returns to PSG from Villa, Fulham agree £30m deal for Charles
Sports.content:
France defender Lucas Digne has completed his return to Paris Saint-Germain from Aston Villa on a three-year contract.

The 33-year-old full-back, who featured in six of Les Bleus’ World Cup matches this summer, had two years left on his contract with the Midlands club, with PSG triggering a reported release clause of between £6m-£7m.

Villa confirmed Digne’s exit on their website, adding that he is “a consummate professional, who was highly regarded by his fellow players and staff alike”.

He made 182 appearances in all competitions for Villa, scoring four goals and making 24 assists, after joining from Everton in a £25m deal in January 2022. He played a key role for Unai Emery’s side as they won the Europa League last season.

The Frenchman made 30 Ligue 1 appearances in a three-year spell at PSG until 2016, when he moved on to Barcelona. He told PSG’s website: “I am very honoured to be returning to Paris Saint-Germain following the wonderful experience I had here more than 10 years ago.”

Fulham have sought to bolster their midfield by spending £30m on Southampton’s Shea Charles.

Charles, a Northern Ireland international and breakout star of the last Championship season, is expected to sign a five-year deal at Craven Cottage once a medical assessment and legal formalities are completed.

View image in fullscreen Shea Charles was a breakout star in the Championship last season, helping Southampton to reach the playoffs. Photograph: Matt Watson/Southampton FC/Getty Images

Fulham will pay an initial fee of £26m, with another £4m dependent on performance, with the size of the fee believed to have ultimately deterred alternative interest from Leeds.

The 22-year-old played 2,000 minutes in the Championship last season as Southampton reached the playoffs before being excluded following revelations of spying against opponents. At Fulham, Charles will be expected to act as the linchpin of the midfield following the sale of Sasa Lukic to Ipswich earlier in the weekend.

Charles joins the young forwards Jonah Kusi-Asare and Gonzalo García as well as 21-year-old attacking midfielder César Palacios on the list of summer signings as Fulham seek to reduce the average age of their squad following the switch of manager from Marco Silva to the former Real Madrid B team coach Álvaro Arbeloa.

Trevoh Chalobah’s move to Como from Chelsea has been confirmed, in a deal worth an initial £25.7m. Terms for a five-year contract were agreed last week, but as the move was announced on Sunday, the England defender said he was “thrilled and honoured” to be joining Cesc Fàbregas’s side.

The pair overlapped at Stamford Bridge towards the end of the Spaniard’s time playing in England, and Chalobah said: “It’s an ambitious, rising project, and working with Cesc Fàbregas again is truly special. I can’t wait to bring my experience to the team, feel the incredible atmosphere at the stadium, and connect with the fans.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Fàbregas said: “Trevoh is a leader who can raise the level of the team, and I am very happy that he has chosen Como.”

Gustavo Hamer has completed a move from the Championship, this time renewing his relationship with Coventry after leaving Sheffield United for a fee of £6m plus add-ons. The Brazilian-born talent will become the Sky Blues’ sixth signing since returning to the top flight, with two big-ticket deals, £24m goalkeeper Carl Rushworth and £25m Ghanaian international midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi, joining in the last week alone.

View image in fullscreen Trevoh Chalobah will be linking up Cesc Fàbregas after joining Como on a five-year deal Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

Hamer was a key part of Mark Robins’s Coventry side as they reached the FA Cup semi-final and Championship playoff final two years ago, only for the attacking midfielder to then leave the club in a £15m deal with the promoted Blades. Following immediate relegation and a misfiring season last term, Hamer will begin a second stint at the CBS Arena, this time under Frank Lampard.

Midfielder Idrissa Gueye has joined Saudi Pro League newcomers Diriyah. The 36-year-old left Everton at the end of last season and arrives at his new club as a free agent. Gueye played in all four of Senegal’s matches at this summer’s World Cup as his country progressed to the last 32.

Elsewhere, Hull completed the signing of the Swedish wing-back Elliot Stroud from Mjallby. The 24-year-old featured in every game for his country at the World Cup and has signed a four-year deal. Reports also continue to link Sporting’s centre-half Ousmane Diomande with a £30m move to Nottingham Forest, with the Ivorian international said to be travelling to the UK from Portugal on Sunday in order to complete his medical. Diomande is understood to be the new Forest manager Oliver Glasner’s first-choice signing, and a player seen as having a key role to play in the German’s preferred 3-4-3 setup.

Sports.title: Formula One star George Russell reveals he's engaged to his long-term girlfriend Carmen Mundt as he shares snaps of stunning candlelit proposal - weeks after hinting at marriage plans
Sports.content:
Formula One star George Russell has revealed he's engaged to his long-term girlfriend Carmen Mundt.

The Mercedes racer shared he proposed to the Spanish businesswoman in a heartfelt social media post.

George shared adorable snaps of the proposal, including one of Carmen showing off her beautiful engagement ring, after he popped the question during a romantic candle-lit dinner.

The official F1 account was among the first congratulate the happy couple, after they got engaged while on a sunny island getaway.

The couple have been together since 2020, with George sharing back in June he was ready to pop the question.

Carmen was born in Spain, and moved to London when she was 18 to study business management and finance from the University of Westminster.

Formula One star George Russell has revealed he's engaged to his long-term girlfriend Carmen Mundt after six years together

The Mercedes racer shared he proposed to the Spanish businesswoman in a heartfelt social media post, as they enjoyed a romantic candlelit dinner

George had previously credited Carmen with helping him to stay grounded as an F1 driver, and described her as his 'future.'

He told The Times: 'Carmen brings me stability when it comes to racing and also a way to disconnect.

'Without doubt she's my future. So [I hope we'll be married] in due course. It won't be next week, but it won't be longer than five years. So somewhere in that timeframe.'

George also said in March: 'I have a really great group of people around me. Carmen is a huge part of that. She supports me in every way possible.

'When I was in Melbourne and preparing to race she got on the time zone, going to bed at six at night and waking up at three in the morning.

'I'm sure some people prefer going out for dinner with their friends instead. But not only does she support me mentally, she's invested in what we're trying to achieve. And that helps a lot. I feel very fortunate.'

The pair met by chance over a meal six years ago, when she did not know he was a Formula One driver.

Now, having quit her high-flying financial job in London to live with Russell in Monaco, she regularly supports him at races.

George shared adorable snaps of the proposal, including one of Carmen showing off her beautiful engagement ring

George first came across fashion influencer Carmen, when the Spaniard had been set to meet a friend of his for a date in 2020.

'My mate couldn't make it, so I thought I'll swing along to see how it goes,' Russell told The Sun.

'She told me she's from the south of Spain and she wouldn't ever expect someone to know the small place she's from.

'I knew exactly where she was from, so it was quite coincidental.'

The pair quickly bonded, with George having spent a significant amount of time in the city of Jerez in southern Spain where Carmen hails from during his karting days.

When the pair celebrated five years together, Carmen detailed her pride in her partner in a post on social media.

She wrote: 'Five years with the most wonderful person I could ever ask for. Forever proud of who you are and what you do.'

Russell sits third in the F1 standings this season, 59 points behind teenage team-mate Kimi Antonelli and nine behind seven-time world champion and Ferrari ace Lewis Hamilton.

Sports.title: Donald Trump whips up LIV Golf fans as he rides around with Gary Player on final day of tournament at his New Jersey course
Sports.content:
President Donald Trump spent the day at his Bedminster golf course once again as LIV Golf played its final round.

Trump was on hand for the LIV Golf New York event toward the end of the rebel tour's season.

The day before, the President was spotted on a golf cart driving around as he was followed by security and his daughter, Ivanka.

On Sunday, he was joined by legendary golfer Gary Player on the cart as they watched the action.

The President also got out of his cart and strolled onto one of the tee boxes, waving to fans and supporters.

It's the second day that Trump has been at the event for the struggling golf circuit.

President Donald Trump was joined by Gary Player during LIV Golf New York's final round

The last round of the tournament was held at Trump's golf course in Bedminster, New Jersey

At one point, the Commander-in-Chief even strolled onto the tee box during the tournament

Trump arrived in the area on Friday evening as Air Force One touched down just before 6:00pm ET.

The Presidential motorcade then shepherded him to the course through a nasty thunderstorm that swept across the Northeastern United States.

Trump has been a longtime supporter of the rebel tour that was formerly backed by the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF).

Earlier this year, the PIF announced they would stop financially supporting LIV Golf after the conclusion of the current season.

Earlier this week, LIV announced they had secured funding for the 2027 season, but little further details were revealed.

Over the course of its existence, LIV Golf has frequented golf courses owned by the President's holding company.

Earlier this year, the tournament was held at Trump National Golf Club in Washington, DC.

LIV has also hosted a Miami event at the Blue Monster course at Trump National Doral in the past.

Eric Trump is pictured with his wife, Lara, and their two children, Luke and Carolina Dorothy

Secret Service agents were on hand to protect the president during his visit to New Jersey

LIV has played at multiple Trump-owned golf courses throughout its existence

The President has previously tried to end the civil war between LIV Golf and the PGA Tour

In the past, Trump has attempted to bring a peaceful conclusion to the civil war between LIV and the PGA Tour.

'I do believe that all of the golfers should be playing against each other. They were viewing something as a monopoly, but it's swaying away. It should be the opposite of a monopoly,' Trump told reporters in April.

'I want to see Rory [McIlroy] playing Bryson DeChambeau. I want to see big Jon Rahm playing Scottie, who is so great. Scottie Scheffler is great.

'They have great players on LIV, but it's almost like people want to see that. That's why the Masters was so good, because you saw everybody together.'

Sports.title: T10 is part of cricket's headlong race to the bottom. But here's why Sussex's proposal for a FIFTH format in an already full to bursting calendar should really concern fans, writes LAWENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
T10 is part of cricket's headlong race to the bottom. But here's why Sussex's proposal for a FIFTH format in an already full to bursting calendar should really concern fans, writes LAWENCE BOOTH

The suggestion by the new chairman of Sussex that a T10 competition may be one way of easing the financial concerns of the non-Hundred counties isn't just a sign of the times. It's a cry for help.

The ECB have insisted all along that the funds raised at last year's auction, when the Hundred was valued at £975million, would bankroll domestic red-ball cricket for a generation – an apparently powerful retort to the traditionalists who fear the tournament will devour England's 18-team domestic set-up.

But the ECB's narrative does not tell the whole story. Far from it. In April, Daily Mail Sport revealed details of a secret meeting at Northamptonshire's Wantage Road involving nine of the 11 non-Hundred-hosting counties.

The mood was gloomy, with the clubs – almost all of them loss-making – worried about the growing divide between them and the seven host counties, a divide they worry will only grow once the Hundred's private investors demand a greater slice of a new TV deal for 2029, and the best players migrate inevitably to the richest clubs.

And while the non-host counties can in theory access around £25million each following the Hundred windfall, that money has to be spent on projects approved by the ECB, such as paying off structured debt or improving infrastructure.

One source who attended the meeting, held without the knowledge of the ECB, said: 'The feeling was that all the clubs are heading to a cliff edge at various speeds. They will all fall over one after the other if something is not addressed in the short term.'

Sussex are proposing a T10 competition to supposedly help non-Hundred hosting counties

And that is where Ed Warner, the new Sussex chair, comes in. Sussex were one of two non-host counties (along with Durham) to miss the secret meeting, and for good reason: they have spent much of the year trying to unravel the financial mess that led to them being placed in special measures, and docked points in all three county competitions.

After telling The Guardian that the Hundred had 'not rescued us in any way, shape or form', Warner captured the mood that day at Wantage Road by considering ways a non-host county might stage more cricket, and make more money, during the Hundred's nearly month-long duration – a period, at the height of summer and during the school holidays, when clubs are staging only four home Metro Bank 50-over matches.

Warner wondered: 'Why couldn't you have a T10 triangular competition with Kent and Essex, for example? Make it very kid-friendly, make it a day at the seaside, then go and play at Canterbury, then go and play in Chelmsford.'

His suggestion, though not itself discussed at the meeting, deserves full marks for lateral thinking. But it should concern cricket lovers on a few counts.

The first is that it would further complicate an already insane schedule, in which the response to the introduction of a fourth format – the Hundred – has been to stage it at the same time as the 50-over competition, diminishing a format in which England are now international also-rans. Our calendar is already full to bursting, without a fifth format trying to elbow its way in.

The second is that T10 feels like part of cricket's headlong race to the bottom. Yes, Abu Dhabi has been hosting its own T10 tournament since 2017, but it has made headlines mainly for reasons of corruption, both proven and alleged. If the Hundred feels like a hurry, T10 is a sprint. What next: F5, or the toss of a coin?

The third concern, and the most significant, is that Warner felt the need to air the suggestion in the first place.

Forget for a moment the financial incompetence at Hove that last week led business management consultancy firm Campbell Tickell to suggest an overhaul of the Sussex board 'as soon as is practically possible'.

The format would complicate an already insane schedule and be part of cricket's headlong race to the bottom

What matters is that the smaller counties are having to countenance alternative means of paying the bills at a time when the ECB tell us the game is richer than ever.

As one chief executive put it at the Northampton meeting, the promise of Hundred money has generated more uncertainty, not less, because of the unknown impact on the next broadcast rights deal.

The ECB will blanch at the idea of counties coming up with their own fifth-format schemes, since it would entail an admission of failure by the board. But Sussex's T10 musings are the symptom of a wider malaise – no matter the repeated insistence that the Hundred will save English cricket.

Unless the ECB get to grips with the smaller clubs' concerns, there will be more desperate ideas where that one came from.

Sports.title: The ORIGINAL spygate: John Terry claims Jose Mourinho showed Chelsea stars rival's training footage on eve of game in new Netflix documentary
Sports.content:
The ORIGINAL spygate: John Terry claims Jose Mourinho showed Chelsea stars rival's training footage on eve of game in new Netflix documentary

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jose Mourinho was spying on opposition teams' training sessions while Southampton manager Tonda Eckert was still playing football for his secondary school team

The now-infamous Spygate, which was broken exclusively by Daily Mail Sport and involved Eckert and his Saints side, stole the headlines for weeks upon weeks back in May.

It saw the Saints expelled from the Championship play-off final, after admitting to spying on Middlesbrough and two other rivals.

But it turns out that former Chelsea boss Mourinho was participating in the incendiary practice long before it became trendy.

That's according to former Chelsea captain John Terry, who has revealed in the new three-part Netflix docu-series titled MOURINHO – which is due to be released on Tuesday – that Mourinho once managed to get hold of footage of a rival's training session during his first season in charge of the Blues.

In the documentary, Terry said: 'I remember, we were due to play Bolton and up on the screen is Bolton's training session from the day before.

The new three-part Netflix docu-series titled MOURINHO has revealed that the former Chelsea boss once got hold of a rival's training session before playing them

John Terry revealed in the documentary that Mourinho got a hold of a Bolton Wanderers training session in his first season at the club.

'And Big Sam [Allardyce] was like "hit Gallas, he's not very good in the air" and he was like spitting on the mic.

'It was just like, wow. Who gets footage from someone's training ground? I'm actually still not sure where he got the footage from.'

It is unclear whether this was ahead of the home or away fixture during that season, in which Chelsea secured their first Premier League title.

If it was ahead of the clash at Stamford Bridge in November 2004, then, much like in the case of Eckert and Southampton, Mourinho's shady tactics failed to have the desired outcome as Chelsea drew 2-2 with Sam Allardyce's side.

However, if the spying was done ahead of the reverse fixture, then it proved fruitful as Chelsea famously secured the title at the then-named Reebok Stadium, with Frank Lampard scoring a brace in a 2-0 win.

The practice of spying has certainly become much more popular in the two decades that have since passed, with Marcelo Bielsa also found to have instructed a colleague to snoop on Derby County's training ahead of a Championship game in 2019.

Leeds were fined £200,000 and reprimanded by the EFL after the club admitted a breach of Regulation 3.4, which states: 'In all matters and transactions relating to the League, each club shall behave towards each other club and The League with the utmost good faith.'

Sports.title: 'There were tears': Frank Lampard and John Terry open up on Jose Mourinho's emotional exit from Chelsea in 2007 as Portuguese coach reveals how his relationship with Roman Abramovich fell apart
Sports.content:
Frank Lampard and John Terry have lifted the lid on the Chelsea squad's emotional reaction to Jose Mourinho's first departure from the club.

Mourinho enjoyed two spells as Blues boss, winning three Premier League titles during his time at the helm.

Two of those titles came during his first tenure at Stamford Bridge, as the self-proclaimed 'Special One' began life in England with back-to-back titles. However, cracks began to appear during his second season in charge.

The new three-part Netflix docu-series titled MOURINHO, which is due to be released on Tuesday, has delved into how Mourinho's first stint at Chelsea unravelled before his eventual sacking in September 2007.

Lampard and Terry were Chelsea's two most important players during Mourinho's glory days, and during the documentary outlined just how much his exit affected them personally, and the squad.

‘I remember him coming into the dressing room and he said to me that he’d been sacked,' Lampard explained.

Frank Lampard (left, pictured in 2005) and John Terry (right) were deeply affected by Jose Mourinho's first departure from Chelsea in 2007

'I couldn’t think about how much this man had helped my career, how much I loved working with him. There were tears, which is not normal in the dressing room when a manager leaves.’

Former Chelsea skipper Terry made much of his adoration for Mourinho known in the documentary, stating that ‘I would leave that pitch in a coffin for him.' And almost two decades on, he puts blame on himself for the manager's exit.

‘You’ve got grown men, tears running down their face, not really understanding why. And even still today I’m like, that’s my fault.

'When we drew the Champions League game [with Rosenborg], my man scored. If I didn’t let that person score, would he have lasted another couple of years? Who knows? I still feel kind of responsible for that, if that makes sense.

'It’s just disappointing how it all ended, if I’m honest. I absolutely loved him and adored him and was more upset than anyone, to be honest.’

Mourinho made it clear that his relationship with then-owner Roman Abramovich had become increasingly fractious as the seasons went by, despite the success the Blues were having on the pitch.

‘In my work, the triangle: Jose, Peter Kenyon (former chief executive), Roman was invaded by strangers.

'In the beginning, you play at Stamford Bridge, you look to the box, Roman, his wife, with one or two persons of his confidence. A few seasons later: former players, agents. These kinds of people, they know where the money is.’

Terry became emotional when talking about Mourinho's exit in the new docu-series about the former Chelsea manager

The documentary also outlined the breakdown in Mourinho's relationship with then-owner Roman Abramovich (pictured in 2004)

The former Chelsea boss also recalled a bizarre incident that affected his relationship with Abramovich, which saw the Russian request him to leave club training to help manage a group of strangers abroad as a favour.

‘I think Roman changed,' Mourinho continued. 'For example, one day Peter came to me quite embarrassed and he told me,"Jose, I have to tell you something.

'"The boss is in Sardinia with these boats, and the people that work in these boats they play football against guys from the hotel, and they are losing. Can you go there to win a game for him?”“No, Peter, I have training today. I have to prepare for tomorrow; I cannot go”.

'And he [Roman] was not happy with that.’

The pair did go on to mend their relationship in the end, with Mourinho turning down the opportunity to become Sir Alex Ferguson's successor at Manchester United in 2013 in order to return to Stamford Bridge.

In the docu-series Mourinho extraordinarily revealed that he verbally agreed to take over at Old Trafford before making a dramatic U-turn in order to re-join the Blues.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho REFUSES to apologise to former Chelsea team doctor Eva Carneiro over infamous 'daughter of a wh***' touchline row as he finally addresses row 11 years later: 'I always use my vocabulary when I'm not happy'
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho REFUSES to apologise to former Chelsea team doctor Eva Carneiro over infamous 'daughter of a wh***' touchline row as he finally addresses row 11 years later: 'I always use my vocabulary when I'm not happy'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jose Mourinho has avoided apologising to Dr Eva Carneiro after opening up about their infamous touchline row for the first time in over a decade.

The former Chelsea boss has spoken about the incident in his new three-part Netflix docu-series titled MOURINHO, which marks the first time he has done so since agreeing a settlement with the club's former doctor in 2016.

During a Premier League clash with Swansea City at the start of the 2015-16 season, Mourinho hit the roof when Carneiro and physio Jon Fearn went onto the pitch to treat Eden Hazard, who had gone down seemingly injured.

Dr Carneiro claimed that Mourinho sexually discriminated against her during his tirade and called her the 'daughter of a wh***' in his native Portuguese.

Back in 2015, Mourinho called her 'impulsive and naive' in his first public reaction to her decision to treat Hazard. She was then dropped from first-team duties and left the club just a month later.

Mourinho and Chelsea eventually agreed a settlement after Carneiro took them to a tribunal over claims that she was discriminated against by the manager, and constructively dismissed by the club.

Jose Mourinho had an infamous touchline spat with Dr Eva Carneiro during a Chelsea match in 2015

The 63-year-old has spoken up about the incident for the first time in over a decade in Netflix's new three-part docu-series MOURINHO

But 11 years on, Mourinho believes he treated Carneiro in the same manner that he would treat a male doctor.

‘For me, a lady doctor is the same as a man’s doctor,' Mourinho said in the docu-series. 'So, as always, I use my vocabulary when I’m not happy.

'There are words in moments where the tension is very, very high. Normally, people with football culture, with football DNA, with football background, they go over it in one second. In that case, it was different.’

Hazard, who played under the now-63-year-old for two years, claimed 'it was nothing special' in the documentary, which is set to air on Tuesday, but 'with Jose everything is bigger'.

Footage shows that the Portuguese coach, who is now Real Madrid manager, shouted a whole host of expletives toward Carneiro and Fearn as they treated Hazard. He screamed phrases such as 'f*** off, man' and 'f*** you, man'.

'I’m not a doctor, but my eyes know when a player is injured, and they know when a player is not injured,' Mourinho said in the docu-series.

'I knew that he was not injured, but the doctors went to the pitch, and in that moment we were left with nine players.’

Hazard was forced to come off the pitch for a brief period, as is the rule when a player receives medical treatment, leaving Chelsea with nine men after Thibaut Courtois had been sent off.

John Terry, who was Chelsea's captain during both of Mourinho's stints at Stamford Bridge, claimed it was well known by both players and staff that the manager did not want his

Speaking in MOURINHO, he said: ‘Medically, he would say unless it’s really, really bad, then they’re [the team doctors] not coming on. That was the understanding for us as players; the medical staff, everyone bought into that.

‘It was a big moment obviously and he took a lot of backlash for that. There was a lot of heat on the football club.’

Carneiro left Chelsea one month after the incident after being dropped from first-team duties

Mourinho agreed a settlement with the club's former doctor after going to tribunal

Chelsea gave Dr Carneiro an unreserved apology, but Mourinho refused to say sorry and grinned as he left the tribunal.

A deal was done in a back corridor of the court and Chelsea then issued a statement saying it 'regretted the circumstances' which led to former club doctor leaving and 'apologises unreservedly to her and her family for the distress caused'.

The terms of the settlement remain secret, but during the tribunal it was revealed that Chelsea had previously offered £1.2million to silence Carneiro.

Mourinho did not apologise after the incident or at the tribunal and there were no signs of an apology in the docu-series either.

The three-part documentary combs through the career of Mourinho, covering the various highs and lows from his three decades in the professional game, from his winning mentality and undeniable ability to secure silverware to his many, many controversies.

Terry and Frank Lampard are just two of a host of Mourinho's former players who provide anecdotes and insight into the manager, who has won 26 major trophies during his career on the touchline.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho makes stunning admission that he AGREED to replace Sir Alex Ferguson as Man United manager in 2013 before making U-turn during emotional phone call with legendary boss
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho has extraordinarily revealed that he 'signed' to become Sir Alex Ferguson's replacement at Manchester United in 2013, before going back on his decision to re-join Chelsea.

Mourinho, 63, managed the Red Devils between 2016 and 2018, but has now admitted for the first time that he agreed to take charge of the club three years prior.

The Portuguese coach had just left Real Madrid in dramatic circumstances and was on the lookout for his next project when he was approached by United and Sir Alex.

Ferguson was looking for his successor after he left the club following a trophy-laden 26 years at the helm, and until now, it was believed that the managerial legend only had eyes for David Moyes.

However, speaking in his new three-part Netflix docu-series, Mourinho dropped the bombshell that he was actually Ferguson's first-choice.

'I go to Chelsea in 2013. But in that period, there is something that nobody knows,' said the now Real Madrid boss in MOURINHO, which is set to air on Tuesday.

Jose Mourinho has revealed he agreed to become Sir Alex Ferguson's replacement at Man United in 2013

The Portuguese coach dropped the bombshell in his new Netflix docu-series titled MOURINHO

'I think I can say because I don't hurt anyone with the truth. And I think the objective of the work that we are doing is to tell the truth. When I left Real Madrid, I signed with Manchester United to go to Manchester United after Sir Alex.'

Following the stunning statement, the documentary then shows Ferguson confirming that he had indeed asked Mourinho to take over from him at United.

Ferguson said: ‘He was offered the job, yes. I sat him down and explained the situation, and as far as I was concerned, he was accepting. And then within hours, it changed.'

Despite seemingly verbally agreeing with Ferguson to become his successor, Mourinho made a dramatic U-turn and instead decided to go back to his former club Chelsea, six years after his initial departure.

'Early evening, he phoned me, and he was crying,' Ferguson continued. He said, “I can’t take it, I’ve given my word to Chelsea, and I’m not going to break my word”.

'The reason he gave to me, I can understand, but I was disappointed.’

Mourinho was coming off the back of a turbulent season at Real Madrid, in which he and various members of the squad had fallen out. Sami Khedira, former Real midfielder and now Mourinho's assistant, even described the dressing room as a 'nightmare' to be a part of.

And that difficult end to his tenure in Madrid, where he has now returned to, played a key part in his decision to return to Chelsea rather than take over at United.

'I was of course very flattered because Man United has an incredible appeal,' Mourinho added. 'When I say Real Madrid is the biggest club in the world, I have to say that Manchester United is very, very close.

'But one thing is love for football, and another thing is love for a certain club. I think this is more powerful than love for football, and fundamentally after Real Madrid, I needed to feel that I’m loved.

Sir Alex Ferguson confirmed Mourinho agreed to be his successor before making a u-turn

Mourinho decided to re-join Chelsea instead and says that he 'did it for love'

‘For me to lose the chance to be the coach to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson was dramatic. But I don’t regret because it was a decision I made with my heart.

'I think it is [Friedrich] Nietzsche (the philosopher) who said something that when you do something for love, you are never doing anything wrong. I did it for love.’

Mourinho ended up spending two years back at the Blues, winning a third Premier League title of his career and a League Cup.

Meanwhile, Ferguson's successor Moyes lasted just nine months in the job, and the Red Devils have yet to win another Premier League since the division's most successful-ever manager left Old Trafford.

Mourinho did eventually end up at United, and managed to win the League Cup and the UEFA Europa League in his first season at the club before leading them to a second-place Premier League finish in 2017-18.

But his tenure quickly unravelled during his third season with poor results and a fallout with several prominent players – including £89million Paul Pogba – led to his sacking in December of his third season.

Sports.title: Everton and Crystal Palace in advanced talks over Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson swap deal - as Trevoh Chalobah joins Como in £25.7m move: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Everton and Crystal Palace in advanced talks over Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson swap deal - as Trevoh Chalobah joins Como in £25.7m move: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Everton and Palace advance in swap deal talks

Everton and Crystal Palace are advancing in talks over a swap deal involving Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil.

Initial discussions last week were described as complicated over the difference in value; Johnson, 25, cost £35million from Tottenham when he joined in January and has four years left on contract.

McNeil, 26, was valued at £20m when he saw a move to Palace collapse in January and has one year remaining on contract.

Everton and Crystal Palace are advancing in talks over a swap deal involving Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil

However, talks between the two clubs are now progressing over a compromise.

Johnson has been a long-term target for Everton and David Moyes, dating back to his spell at Nottingham Forest. He joined Palace for a then-club record transfer fee, in the winter window but has struggled badly to find any form and there is a growing sense a move would suit all parties.

McNeil was upset when he failed to get his move away in January but regained his place under Moyes. If all goes well a deal both players could be given permission to undergo medicals early this week.

Meanwhile, Palace are keen to offer a new contract for Jefferson Lerma while Club Brugge are pushing to agree a £10m deal plus sell-on for Pakace's Romain Esse.

Digne returns to PSG

France defender Lucas Digne has completed his return to Paris St Germain from Aston Villa on a three-year contract.

The 33-year-old full-back, who featured in six of Les Bleus' World Cup matches, had two years left on his contract with the midlands club, with PSG triggering a release clause.

Digne, who started his professional career with Lille, made 30 Ligue 1 appearances in a three-year spell at PSG until 2016, when he moved on to Barcelona.

France defender Lucas Digne has completed his return to Paris St Germain from Aston Villa

He told PSG's website: 'I am very honoured to be returning to Paris St Germain following the wonderful experience I had here more than 10 years ago.

'I am particularly impressed by how the club has developed over the years. The working conditions at the Campus are exceptional and reflect the club's ambitions.

'I can't wait to start this new chapter and put all my experience at the service of the team. Once again, I will give my very best to defend the colours of Paris St Germain.'

JAMES DUTTON

Chalobah's Italian Job

Trevoh Chalobah has completed his move from Chelsea to Italian side Como in a deal worth more than £30million.

England defender Chalobah departs Stamford Bridge for an initial £25.7m plus a further £5.1m in potential add-ons, as revealed by Window Watch last week.

The 27-year-old has signed a contract until 2031 with the Serie A club, who are managed by former Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas and are preparing for their first season in the Champions League.

Trevoh Chalobah has completed his move from Chelsea to Italian side Como in a deal worth more than £30million

Chalobah made 151 appearances for the Blues, including 47 last term, after joining the club's academy at under-nine level.

He said: 'I'm thrilled and honoured to be here at Como. It's an ambitious, rising project and working with manager Cesc Fabregas again is truly special.

'I can't wait to bring my experience to the team, feel the incredible atmosphere at the stadium, and connect with the fans. I will give my absolute all every single day to make history together'.

JAMES DUTTON

Sunderland target Ipswich keeper

Sunderland are showing interest in Ipswich Town goalkeeper Alex Palmer.

The 29-year-old has emerged as an option for Regis Le Bris' side as Wrexham continue to push for Sunderland keeper Anthony Patterson who is valued at £8m.

Palmer is also on Wrexham's radar should a deal for Patterson fall down.

Ipswich face Sunderland in the first game of the season.

As well as Palmer, Ipswich have Christian Walton returning from injury and have signed two new Dutch keepers in Kjell Scherpen and Kayne van Oevelen.

The latter may yet go out on loan and Ipswich are among the clubs that have held interest in Newcastle United keeper Nick Pope.

Man City striker in talks with Southampton

Manchester City striker Divin Mubama has agreed to join Southampton on loan for the season.

The former West Ham forward did well on loan at Stoke City last season up until he suffered an ankle ligament injury in January, incurred by a hefty challenge against QPR.

Manchester City striker Divin Mubama has agreed to join Southampton on loan for the season

He has bounced back to full fitness though and has impressed on City's pre-season tour scoring two goals, including a composed finish against Inter Milan, and weighing in with an assist.

The 21-year-old has had interest from a number of Championship clubs including Preston North End, Middlesbrough and Derby County.

Swedish international heads to Hull

Hull City have signed Sweden international Elliot Stroud from Swedish side Mjallby for around £3.5million.

The wing-back has joined on a four-year contract, which includes an option for a an extra year.

The 24-year-old played in all four of Sweden's matches at the World Cup.

West Ham make opening Parrott bid

West Ham have made an opening offer understood to be worth around £15million for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott

West Ham have made an opening offer understood to be worth around £15million for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott and are exploring a deal for Arsenal's Reiss Nelson.

Parrott, their leading goalscorer last season, started on the bench for Alkmaar's opening league game against Den Haag on Saturday.

The Hammers are prepared to break the Championship record of over £17.5million to get Parrott amid competition from Porto.

Nelson has been on the Hammers' radar before and has attracted interest from Fulham and Benfica in this window.

The 26-year-old had an indifferent campaign on loan at Brentford last season.

The Hammers had been pursuing a loan for Sunderland's Simon Adingra but he picked up an injury and has been wearing a protective boot on his left foot.

United keen on Page

Manchester United are interested in signing Leicester prospect Louis Page.

The 18-year-old midfielder has made 21 appearances for the Foxes and won EFL Apprentice of the Year last season.

Arsenal and Aston Villa have also expressed interest in the England Under-20 international but it is understood he wants to join United.

Louis Page has impressed for Leicester and is on the radar of some top sides

Charles closes on Fulham move

Fulham have agreed a £30million deal with Southampton for midfielder Shea Charles.

The 22-year-old is expected to undergo a medical in the next 24 hours and will sign a five-year contract with the option for an extra year.

Read the full story here.

Willock on Besiktas radar

Newcastle midfielder Joe Willock remains a target for Besiktas.

The Turkish side are working on an offer for the 26-year-old but believe Newcastle's current asking price is too high.

Joe Willock is a target of Turkish side Besiktas this month

Newcastle are continuing to work on a £13m deal for Marseille's Pierre Emile Hojbjerg.

They want an experienced midfielder to work alongside new signings Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba.

Read the latest on Newcastle's summer transfer business here.

Race to sign Tuanzebe heats up

Free agent defender Axel Tuanzebe is attracting interest from Saudi Pro league and Premier League sides.

The 28-year-old centre back had an impressive World Cup on the back of a challenging season with Burnley in the top flight and is ready for a new challenge.

Axel Tuanzebe is drawing a lot of interest from both English sides and abroad

Everton and Brentford have looked at the former Manchester United academy graduate and he has drawn attention from abroad also.

He made 16 appearances and scored one goal last season and spent the two previous seasons with Ipswich Town.

Hamer closes on Cov return

Gus Hamer is due to undergo a medical after Coventry and Sheffield United agreed a £6million deal for the midfielder.

The package for the 29-year-old is worth £6m plus add-ons.

Hamer spent three years at Coventry between 2020 and 2023, becoming a real fans favourite scoring 19 goals in 132 appearances.

Blades manager Chris Wilder hinted last week that Hamer had asked to join Coventry and had already spoken to Frank Lampard. His medical is scheduled for today.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho's tearful phone call with Man Utd manager and Roman Abramovich feud revealed
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho cried on the phone to Sir Alex Ferguson as he confirmed his decision to not replace him at Manchester United. Instead, he ended up returning to Chelsea despite seeing his relationship with Roman Abramovich fall apart during his first Stamford Bridge stint.

Those are just some of the bombshell reveals made in the new Netflix docuseries, 'Mourinho', which airs on Tuesday. The show is set to drop just as 'The Special One' prepares for an even more audacious comeback at Real Madrid, 13 years after he left on terrible terms.

Mourinho, 63, was public enemy No. 1 when he first left Los Blancos in 2013, having lost the support of his dressing room and the media. That same summer, he had agreed to take over at Old Trafford when Ferguson retired - before backing out of the deal.

"He was offered the job, yes," said Ferguson. "I sat him down and explained the situation and, as far as I was concerned, he was accepting. And then, within hours, had changed."

‌



Mourinho recalled: "I was, of course, very flattered, because Man United has an incredible appeal. When I say Real Madrid is the biggest club in the world, I have to say that Man United is very, very close.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Jose Mourinho’s three things he wants from Vinicius Jr as Arsenal transfer outcome awaits READ MORE :

"But one thing is love for football, and another thing is love for a certain club. I think this is more powerful than love for football. And fundamentally, after Real Madrid, I needed to feel I am loved."

Ferguson didn't hide his disappointment that the move never came to pass, especially after they had a tentative agreement in place. But it wasn't a choice that came easily to Mourinho, who became tearful as he informed a peer he respects so much of his decision.

‌



"Early evening, he phoned me and he was crying," Ferguson continued. "And he says, 'Alex, I can't take it. I've given my word to Chelsea and I'm not gonna break my word'. The reason he gave to me, I could understand. But I was disappointed."

Regardless, Mourinho said he harboured no regret over his choice as he clarified: "For me to lose the chance to be the coach to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson was...dramatic. But I don't regret [it], because it was a decision I made with my heart."

View 3 Images Mourinho had agreed to replace Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United in 2013 but backed out of the deal (Image: Matthew Peters/Manchester United via Getty Images)

He ultimately rejoined Chelsea, which was a peculiar decision in itself given his chequered history with the club. Or more specifically former owner Abramovich, who was the focus of his ire when he returned to Stamford Bridge for the first time in the opposition dugout.

‌



Inter Milan's visit to Chelsea in the Champions League's last 16 back in 2010 was the first time Mourinho faced his old team as an enemy. And the nature of his fallout with Abramovich a little more than two years prior made things all too personal.

"Honestly, I was playing against Roman in that game," said Mourinho as he remembered that run-in with his former boss. "I was not playing against Chelsea. I was not playing against the boys. I was playing against him."

Every subscription now comes with 135 channels alongside free subscriptions to HBO Max, Netflix, Disney+, discovery+ and Hayu.

It's ironic that it was Samuel Eto'o who scored the goal that separated the two teams in that second leg and sent Inter through. Mourinho wanted the Cameroonian when he was at Chelsea, only for Abramovich to take the reins and complete a deal for infamous flop Andriy Shevchenko instead.

‌



"That game for me was beauty," Mourinho continued. "I was playing against a guy that sacked me. It felt like pleasure.

"I go home happy and he goes upset, because I know how much he loves Chelsea, I know how much he loves to win. But I needed revenge. Because football belongs to people like me. The other ones are the intruders who don't belong.

"Football belongs to the players, belongs to the coaches, belongs to the fans. Football will always belong to us."

View 3 Images Roman Abramovich enjoyed a period of dominance as Chelsea owner after hiring Mourinho before things took a turn (Image: Getty Images Europe)

‌



There's more than a hint of resentment in those words. It's painstakingly obvious throughout the Netflix series that Mourinho is all-consumed by football but views some of those more accustomed to dealing in boardrooms as little more than interlopers.

The tactician repaired his relationship with Abramovich enough that he returned to Chelsea for a second spell and even won a third Premier League title at the club. It wasn't long, however, before things came crashing down once more and ended with another premature exit.

Mourinho is targeting another redemption arc in a glittering career as he returns to the Bernabeu this summer. And in Florentino Perez, he has another volatile chairman figure he needs to keep onside if this chapter is to be any more successful than the first.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Real Madrid transfer twist as fresh stance on forward’s future explained
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Real Madrid transfer twist as fresh stance on forward’s future explained

Arsenal are looking to strengthen their squad in the transfer market and continue to be linked with possible deals ahead of deadline day on September 1

View 2 Images Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta will face many important transfer decisions before deadline day (Image: Gongora/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Arsenal face a busy few weeks in the transfer window as the new season approaches. Mikel Arteta’s side will hope to pick up where they left off next term after clinching the Premier League and narrowly missing out on the Champions League trophy.

‌



The Gunners have already added to their title-winning side, with former Club Brugge star Christos Tzolis bolstering Arsenal’s wide options. The club also recently completed a £75million move for Bruno Guimaraes as Arteta looked to strengthen in midfield.

‌



In terms of outgoings, Leandro Trossard has joined Besiktas and Christian Norgaard has left for Everton. However, the arrival of Guimaraes has led to speculation over Martin Zubimendi’s future at the Emirates Stadium.

‌



The Spain international signed from Real Sociedad last summer but now faces competition from Guimaraes and countryman Mikel Merino for a regular spot next to Declan Rice. Meanwhile, Gabriel Martinelli has been linked with a possible move to Galatasaray. Here, Mirror Football looks at the biggest transfer stories surrounding the Gunners.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Diego Simeone confirms Julian Alvarez transfer 'decision' amid Arsenal interest READ MORE :

Arsenal face Real Madrid transfer twist

Arsenal face another possible transfer battle with Real Madrid following reports regarding Martin Zubimendi’s future. The Gunners recently targeted Los Blancos star Vinicius Junior before the winger signed a new contract and the sides could soon cross paths again over another player.

‌



Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo reports that Madrid may look to take advantage of Zubimendi’s "uncertain" future at Arsenal following the signing of Guimaraes. The La Liga side look set to miss out on a move for Manchester City’s Rodri and could turn their attention to the Gunners star.

Chelsea are also said to be interested in the 27-year-old, who started 34 league games for Arteta's side last term. Mundo Deportivo claims that Arsenal would demand a minimum of £77m for the midfielder.

Arsenal reportedly beat Madrid to Zubimendi’s signature when completing a £55m move last year. The former Real Sociedad star has since enjoyed a memorable 12 months, winning the Premier League and the World Cup.

‌



View 2 Images Martin Zubimendi was part of Spain's World Cup-winning squad this summer (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



football.london reports that Martinelli currently remains part of Arteta’s plans. However, the club’s pursuit of Vinicius Junior has alerted other sides to his possible availability.

They're unlikely to allow him to join the Turkish side while they continue to hunt for a potential signing. But should they find such a player, then the door will open to a possible exit.

Sports.title: Arsenal star Max Dowman produces telling reaction to Viktor Gyokeres miss in surprise loss
Sports.content:
Arsenal star Max Dowman produces telling reaction to Viktor Gyokeres miss in surprise loss

Arsenal were beaten by Borussia Dortmund in pre-season and teenager Max Dowman showed his frustration after a Viktor Gyokeres miss in the first-half

View 2 Images Viktor Gyokeres scored in Arsenal's pre-season loss, but also missed a major chance

Arsenal's Max Dowman couldn't hide his frustration after seeing Viktor Gyokeres blaze over after laying on his Arsenal team-mate during their loss to Borussia Dortmund.

‌



The Gunners were beaten 3-2 by the German side in front of their own fans in what was less than ideal preparation before they begin their Premier League defence. Dortmund raced into a two-goal lead and, after seeing Ethan Nwaneri pull one back, re-established their two-goal buffer.

‌



Gyokeres scored from the spot to set up a grandstand finish, but earlier in the contest had seen an effort from no more than 12 yards go firing over the bar.

‌



It was Dowman who had made the run to the byline before setting the ball back for the Swede, and after seeing him spurn the opportunity the teenage sensation was caught throwing his arms up in the air in frustration.

Rusty Arsenal lose again as Dortmund defeat exposes Mikel Arteta concern - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Gyokeres, who was able to score from the penalty spot, did cop criticism in his debut season for his finishing. He managed to score 21 times for the Gunners but still question marks hang over whether the ex-Sporting Lisbon star is the forward that Mikel Arteta has been looking for.

When it came to the business end of the season last term Arteta opted to start Kai Havertz as the central point of Arsenal's attack, picking the German over Gyokeres in the Champions League final.

‌



Arsenal had been linked with a lucrative move for Vinicius Junior earlier this summer, but the Brazilian has chosen to remain at Real Madrid. Nevertheless the north Londoners could still go after a blockbuster deal in the final third before the transfer window closes.

View 2 Images Max Dowman was visibly frustrated after seeing his striker blaze his shot over

Arteta said after their loss to Dortmund: "It has to be the right player in the market to make us much better. We are very much looking forward to that."

‌



The Arsenal boss though is adamant that the team will come good despite some below par results in pre-season. "I think it has to, it has to hurt when you lose a football match, it has to hurt when it is a friendly match, a test or whatever you want to call it," he said.

"But yes, we know where we are. We know that we are missing still a lot of players and some players that haven't had enough training. And yes, sometimes it's good."

Sports.title: Arsenal pushing for more signings as Mikel Arteta tells fans club are 'looking forward'
Sports.content:
Arsenal pushing for more signings as Mikel Arteta tells fans club are 'looking forward'

Mikel Arteta has been asked if fans can expect more signings before the transfer window closes with Arsenal still in the market for a new defender

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has admitted Arsenal are in the market for more signings (Image: Carlos Jasso/AFP)

Mikel Arteta has admitted that Arsenal are pushing to sign more players before the end of the transfer window.

‌



The Gunners have spent more than £100million on new players this summer. Piero Hincapie's loan move from Bayer Leverkusen has been made permanent in a £34.5m deal, Christos Tzolis made the £34m switch from Club Brugge, Illan Meslier has signed after his Leeds contract expired, and Bruno Guimaraes has joined for £75m from Newcastle.

‌



But Arsenal, who go into the season as the reigning Premier League champions, are not expected to stop there and want to bolster their squad with more additions in the coming weeks. Indeed, following the Gunners' 3-2 pre-season defeat to Borussia Dortmund on Saturday, Arteta revealed the club remain active in the summer window.

‌



Arsenal respond to Gabriel Martinelli transfer approach as Mikel Arteta lays out demands READ MORE :

Arsenal's champion squad will leave Mikel Arteta having to digest harsh reality READ MORE :

"Well, that's what we're trying to do [sign more players]," Arteta said. "If we have the right player in the market to make us much better. We are very looking forward to that."

Arsenal have conceded six goals in their last two pre-season matches; three against Dortmund and then three in the 3-1 defeat to Real Betis last Wednesday. In both matches, the Gunners looked open at the back and in truth Dortmund and Betis could have scored more than three each.

View 2 Images Jurrien Timber and William Saliba are still out (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



Although it is just pre-season, concerns have been raised about Arsenal's capabilities in defence without William Saliba and Jurrien Timber, with Cristhian Mosquera and Ben White both struggling in the Betis and Dortmund matches. Ezri Konsa has been listed as a top target as the Gunners look to strengthen at the back, though Aston Villa are determined to keep the £35million-rated England international.

When asked if a defender is a position the Gunners are trying to sign, Arteta added: "I wouldn't go there just to put an isolated there. We conceded some poor goals the other day, some poor goals today.

‌



"In the way we competed, especially. But that's a very collective responsibility. So, we need to improve with the players that we have. And we want to improve for sure."

Arsenal go up against Como in their fourth pre-season fixture on Wednesday. They then face Manchester City in the Community Shield next Sunday before their Premier League curtain-raiser against Coventry City.
